transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I suppose I'm here because I'm having some trouble with... my thoughts lately. Just unwanted thoughts. 

I work with data, and I keep getting this feeling that I’ve missed something critical. Like I've put a wrong number in a data release, or... even something at home, like leaving the back door unlocked or paying a bill from the wrong account. 

Even when I know I've already checked it, my mind just... it won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some sort of disaster. It's just getting hard to deal with.
Would you say these thoughts are popping into your mind without you intentionally thinking about them?

Yes... um, I'm definitely not trying to think about them. They just... happen. 

Like I said, they're just unwanted. I'll just be working, or sitting at home, and suddenly my mind is back on the numbers, or the locks. I don't bring it up on purpose. It just forces its way in.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to get rid of these unwanted thoughts?

Um... yes. I suppose I do. Just to... calm myself down, I guess. 

I end up reopening spreadsheets. Or rereading emails... line by line. And with the other things, I... I check the locks, or the payment confirmations. Over and over. I sort of have to do it in a set order, until it finally feels... safe. 

It's... well, some nights I’m still sitting at my desk hours later, and... I have nothing actually finished.
When you repeat these actions, like reopening spreadsheets or checking the locks, are you trying to prevent something bad from happening?

Um... yes. I suppose so. 

Like I mentioned, I just... I have to do those checks until it feels safe. If I don't go through the spreadsheets or the locks in that exact order... I just feel like it's going to cause some sort of disaster. 

That's... well, that's why I end up stuck at my desk all night. Just trying to make sure nothing bad happens.
Do you feel anxious or uncomfortable when you can't perform these repetitive actions?

Yes... very much so. 

If I can't... do the things I mentioned, like checking the locks or going through the spreadsheets and emails... I just feel this awful tension. Like I said, I have to do it in that specific order, over and over, until it feels safe. 

If I try to stop before that... the feeling just gets worse. That's why I end up stuck at my desk for hours. I just... I can't calm down until I finish it.
Do you feel like these repetitive actions you're doing are directly helping to get rid of the unwanted thoughts?

I... I suppose so. At least for a minute. 

Like I've been saying, I just go through the spreadsheets and the emails, and check the locks and the payments... in that same order... just to calm myself down. To make it feel safe so the thoughts will stop. 

But... well, considering I'm usually still sitting there hours later with nothing actually finished... maybe it doesn't really get rid of them. I just... I don't know what else to do.
Do you feel like the actions you repeat have to be done in a very specific way, or that there's something uncomfortable about not doing them that way?

Yes... like I said, it has to be in a set order. 

I have to reopen the spreadsheets, reread my emails line by line... check the locks and the payment confirmations. Over and over, exactly like that. If I do it differently, or skip something... it doesn't feel safe. It's very uncomfortable. 

I just have to keep doing it until the feeling stops. Which is... well, why I'm still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished.
Do you feel like doing these actions in this specific order reduces your anxiety?

I mean... yes. It's supposed to. 

That's why I do it. I just... I reopen the spreadsheets. I reread the emails line by line. I check the locks, the payment confirmations... in that order. I do it to calm myself down. To make it feel safe. 

But... like I said, it doesn't always work right away. Some nights I'm just... still at my desk hours later. And I haven't actually finished any real work. So... I don't know if it really reduces it. But I have to try.
Are you trying to prevent something specific from happening when you repeat these actions?

I don't... I don't know if it's one specific thing. 

I just... like I keep saying, I have to do it all in that set order. The spreadsheets, the emails, the locks, the payments. I just... I do it to calm myself down. To make it feel... safe. 

If I don't do it, it just... feels wrong. Dangerous, I guess. So I keep doing it until that feeling stops. Even if it takes hours.
Do you think your repetitive checking is mainly because you're afraid of making a mistake?

I suppose so, yes. I just... I get these awful, unwanted thoughts that I’ve missed something critical. 

Like... a wrong number in a data release at work. Or an unlocked back door, or a bill paid from the wrong account. And even when I know I've already checked it... my mind just won’t let go of the possibility that I’ve caused some kind of disaster. So... yes. I guess I am afraid of that.
Are these repetitive checks and actions affecting your ability to complete tasks at work or your daily routines at home?

I suppose it is. 

I've... fallen behind on some major deadlines at work. I stay late reviewing things, but I still don't finish. And... I guess it affects my time at home, too. I've stopped going to my salsa nights. Or kayaking. 

I just... I can't seem to get away from all the checking and reviewing in time to actually go. So I just don't.
Are these habits of checking and repeating actions affecting your relationships with friends or family?

I don't really know. 

I mean... I live alone, so... there's not really anyone here for it to bother. And my friends... I don't see them as much since I stopped going out. So... I guess they don't really see it.
Do you feel like these unwanted thoughts and repetitive actions are causing you a lot of distress?

I... I suppose so. 

I try not to dwell on how it makes me feel, honestly. It's just... tiring, mostly. I don't really know what else to say about it.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking actions at specific times of the day or in specific situations?

I guess... mostly when I'm working, or closing up for the night. 

I just... to calm myself down, I end up reopening my spreadsheets. I reread my emails, line by line. Or I check the locks... and payment confirmations. Over and over. I have to do it in a set order, just... until it feels safe. 

And then... well, some nights I'm still sitting at my desk hours later, and I haven't actually finished anything.
Are you avoiding social situations because of these unwanted thoughts and repetitive actions?

I suppose so. 

I just... I don't have the time anymore. I used to go to salsa nights, or... kayaking on the weekends. But I can't really get away from the checking in time to go. 

And... well, I've fallen pretty far behind on my major work deadlines, too. Because I stay so late reviewing everything, but... I still don't actually finish. So, going out just... isn't really an option right now.
